title: PODCAST MREŽNICA: Andrijanić: Berlin wants control of Poland, Tusk has an assignment. This is a lesson for Croatia as well

reels.title: President of Poland pushes through the police to the Constitutional Court
reels.hook: The president goes through the police cordon. First.
reels.why: An eyewitness describes the dramatic scene step by step: the limousine, the crowd, the frightened police officers, physical contact with the judge. It ends with a striking sentence that, according to the guest, Nawrocki said to the security guards.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: Leave that to me, I will take care of it.

cards.text: The president goes through the police cordon. First.
Goran Andrijanić · Croatian-Polish journalist, Warsaw
Warsaw, after the government sent police into the Constitutional Court.
Constitutional Court
Those were young, poor, frightened police officers who had no idea at all why they were there.
“Leave that to me, I will take care of it.”

reels.title: Over Gibraltar he found out about the police in the court and turned the plane around
reels.hook: He found out in the air. And turned the plane around.
reels.why: A movie-like plot with a concrete setting and tension: the presidential aircraft turns back, people track it on radar, and speculations circulate about rerouting the flight.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: That was over Gibraltar. The guy, meaning the president, turns, turns the aircraft around

cards.text: He found out in the air. And turned the plane around.
Goran Andrijanić · Croatian-Polish journalist, Warsaw
President Karol Nawrocki was then flying on a state visit to Senegal.
Over Gibraltar
The president turns the aircraft around, returns back to Poland.
Speculations: they allegedly wanted to divert the flight to Wrocław or Kraków.

reels.title: How the Polish public television was taken over
reels.hook: Television is working, and officially it is in liquidation
reels.why: A journalist from the newsroom recounts the moment the broadcast was interrupted and private security guards raided. The absurdity of a television station that is working while formally in liquidation is a hook in itself.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: the entire public media outlet is at this moment formally in liquidation

cards.text: Television is working, and officially it is in liquidation
Goran Andrijanić · Croatian-Polish journalist, Warsaw
It is about the government of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk.
Takeover of the public television TVP
The police did not raid immediately then, but private security guards raided.
The entire public media outlet is at this moment formally in liquidation.

reels.title: “Today Georgia, tomorrow Ukraine”: Lech Kaczyński's sentence
reels.hook: Said in 2008. Today it sounds like a prophecy.
reels.why: A short, self-contained story with a clear location, year, and a quote that, according to the guest, came true. A powerful hook for anyone following the war in Ukraine.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: Today Georgia, tomorrow Ukraine, and the day after tomorrow the Baltic states or perhaps even my homeland.

cards.text: Said in 2008. Today it sounds like a prophecy.

War in Georgia
Tbilisi
Lech Kaczyński, Polish president, died in 2010 in an accident near Smolensk.
“Today Georgia, tomorrow Ukraine, and the day after tomorrow the Baltic states or perhaps even my homeland.”

reels.title: Russophobia? Poles remember the massacre of 30,000 civilians near Warsaw
reels.hook: Poles are not Russophobes. They have a reason.
reels.why: A clear question and answer with a concrete historical event and figure. A little-known story shatters a common stereotype.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: Russian generals slaughtered somewhere around thirty thousand civilians without any war.

cards.text: Poles are not Russophobes. They have a reason.

Part of Warsaw on the other side of the Vistula
civilians killed

reels.title: German soldiers in Greenland and a lesson for Croatia: arm yourself
reels.hook: Can Europe defend anyone at all?
reels.why: A humorous image of German soldiers fleeing from the weather in Greenland leads to a clear, practical stance for Croatia. Short, self-contained, and provocative.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: Europe at this moment does not have military capacities with which it can match anyone.

cards.text: Can Europe defend anyone at all?

Prime Minister Tusk relies on the EU, President Nawrocki on the USA.
Greenland

reels.title: Why are Croatian conservatives silent about the crisis in Poland?
reels.hook: Police in the Constitutional Court, while the Croatian right is silent
reels.why: Direct criticism of named Croatian parties, with a clear message that the same can happen in Croatia tomorrow. For the local audience, this is provocative and relatable.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: here it is about a situation that is in its essence universal and that can happen tomorrow in Croatia.

cards.text: Police in the Constitutional Court, while the Croatian right is silent

reels.title: Tusk, Vučić, and the same mentor: Angela Merkel
reels.hook: What do Tusk and Vučić have in common?
reels.why: It begins with a rhetorical question and a concrete explanation about German scholarships, and ends with an unexpected connection to Vučić and a witty interjection by the host.
reels.speaker: Goran Andrijanić
reels.quote: political child of Angela Merkel, who was his mentor from the very beginnings.
